pages.rawText: 16 A class of students are developing a program to send data between computers. Many computers 8 are connected together to form a wired network. Serial ports are used to connect one computer to another. Each computer: is assigned a unique three-digit ID • has three ports, each identified by an integer value • is connected to between one and three other computers. • Data is sent as individual message strings. Each string contains the destination ID (the ID of the computer that is to receive the message) followed by the data: <DestinationID><Data> Messages may pass through several computers on the way to their destination. When a message arrives at a computer, that is the destination, the program needs to forward not it on to another computer using one of its serial ports. The port to use is obtained from information that is stored in an array . RouteTable is a global 2D array of integers. It is declared in pseudocode as follows: RouteTable DECLARE RouteTable : ARRAY[1:6,1:3] OF INTEGER The values in the first two columns of define a range of ID values. RouteTable Column 3 gives the corresponding port number to use when forwarding the message to a computer with an ID within this range. For example, the contents of could be: RouteTable Column 1 Column 2 Column 3 Row 1 100 199 1 Row 2 200 259 2 Row 3 −1 <undefined> <undefined> Row 4 260 399 2 Row 5 400 599 3 Row 6 600 999 1 In this example, a message that arrives with a of "283" will be forwarded using DestinationID port 2. Row 3 in the example shows an unused row. These may occur anywhere. Unused rows have the column 1 element set to −1. The value of unused elements in the other two columns is undefined. © UCLES 2023 9618/22/O/N/23
